title: Audit — every write made on your behalf

data.name: entries
data.shape: AuditEntry[] — { createdAt, tool, destructive, actor, outcome, failureReason, platformDestructiveHint }

components.purpose: Show every operation Grid-Commander performed on the account, who caused it, and how it ended.
components.current_implementation: Unstyled table in an overflow-x-auto wrapper, sr-only caption, four columns. Empty state is a single sentence. Styled with Tailwind (3.4.19, installed since this surface was first surveyed).
constraints: `attempted` must never be styled as a failure. It means an operation started and we never learned how it ended — which is exactly what an audit log should say, and collapsing it into 'failed' loses the distinction that makes the log trustworthy

'you' and 'the assistant, answering you' are different levels of intent and must stay distinct. `actor-assistant` is now historical-only — nothing can write an assistant row since the assistant's removal (`only-mcp-control`) — but the state must keep rendering: rows from before the removal exist, and collapsing the branch would render them as 'you', a false statement about who acted on the one surface whose entire job is saying who acted

`destructive` is marked with a word, not only a colour or icon — colour is never the only signal. **`destructive` states this product’s judgement, not the platform’s** (#340, 2026-08-17). Where BattleGrid positively disagreed — our `true` against its `false` — the row also carries the plain-text note “(platform says otherwise)” with the explanation in a `title`. `platformDestructiveHint: null` means the claim was **not recorded**, which is every row written before that date; it is never read as agreement and draws nothing. A design must not resolve the disagreement by hiding one side of it.
The unresolved-count banner is role=status and must not block or obscure the table
The table must remain a real table with its caption and column scopes; it is the one screen users will read down a column
Timestamps must stay machine-readable in `<time datetime>` regardless of display format
The empty state must keep promising future entries rather than reading as an error

components.purpose: Turn away a request with no authority.
components.current_implementation: Shared component rendered in place of the page body.
constraints: One page for every cause (design W-C)

accessibility.notes: Table has an sr-only caption and scoped column headers. Unresolved count is role=status. Horizontal scroll is on a wrapper so the table itself is not clipped.
